disposition.quote: Results replicated the four patterns of negative emotional eating ... in previous research, including non-emotional eating (non-EE), emotional over- and under-eating (EOE-EUE),

worker_target_description: Xu et al. (2024), general Chinese adults; four-class emotional eating LCA and class comparisons. Exact outcome/contrast for this row remains ambiguous.
worker_notes: Both assigned rows have identical neutral descriptions, p.4 locators, and study identifiers. No outcome or contrast distinguishes them. No row-order or numeric matching used. The replication is general Chinese adults aged 18–75 (Table 1), rather than the original young adults aged 17–24 in the description. Candidate critical tests on p.4 section 3.5: typical eating disorder symptomatology omnibus chi-square 47.78, p < .001; muscularity-oriented eating disorder symptomatology omnibus chi-square 50.40, p < .001; psychosocial impairment omnibus chi-square 115.88, p < .001; emotion regulation difficulties omnibus chi-square 128.12, p < .001. Typical symptomatology pairwise candidates: EOE versus EOE-EUE chi-square 8.29, p = .004, d = .39; EOE versus EUE chi-square 27.02, p < .001, d = .69; EOE versus non-EE chi-square 40.98, p < .001, d = .92. Muscularity symptomatology pairwise candidates: EOE versus non-EE chi-square 30.87, p < .001, d = .84; EOE versus EUE chi-square 31.79, p < .001, d = .81; EOE-EUE versus non-EE chi-square 18.41, p < .001, d = .56; EOE-EUE versus EUE chi-square 18.81, p < .001, d = .51; EOE versus EOE-EUE chi-square 3.58, p = .058, d = .27. There are additional pairwise psychosocial impairment and emotion regulation tests on pp.4–5, sex-membership odds ratios in section 3.4, and LCA fit comparisons in Table 2. None is uniquely assigned by these locators. Candidate common sample only: Table 1 n = 600 and section 2.1 final 600 adults after 33 validity-test exclusions. Participant role; no separately stated row-specific analytic N assigned. No N inferred from df, percentages, or summed recruitment groups. Authors report successful replication of the four latent patterns; this is a paper-level narrative verdict, not confirmation that each unidentified contrast replicated. Discussion p.5 calls typical-symptomatology findings partially consistent with hypotheses. PDF pp.4–5 rendered and visually inspected for column and table layout. Original is an unassigned placeholder, not a claim that the original paper is unavailable.

prior_adjudication.location: p. 1, Abstract; p. 4, Section 3.5; p. 5, Section 4
prior_adjudication.quote: were found in typical eating disorder symptomatology (χ 2 = 47.78,
prior_adjudication.reason: The neutral locator (broad LCA description and p. 4) is identical across rows 249 and 250 and does not uniquely identify a single target outcome among the multiple p. 4 analyses (class-solution fit comparisons in Table 2, sex-difference multinomial regressions, and omnibus/pairwise BCH group comparisons across "eating disorder symptomatology, psychosocial impairment, and emotion regulation difficulties."). Furthermore, the global abstract statement "Results replicated the four patterns of negative emotional eating" applies to the four-class LCA structure rather than specific outcome tests (where class rankings were only "partially consistent with the hypotheses" and psychosocial impairment was an expansion measure not in He et al., 2020), and numerical coincidence with the coded chi-square cannot establish target identity.

prior_adjudication.reason: As in row 249, the neutral p. 4 locator and original-study description do not uniquely map this row to a specific test among the multiple p. 4 group comparisons without relying on numerical coincidence with the coded statistic. In addition, the paper states that "prior studies did not examine group differences in muscularity-oriented eating disorder symptomatology (Dixit et al., 2023; He et al., 2020) or psychosocial impairment (He et al., 2020)" and that EOE versus EOE-EUE showed "no significant difference between the EOE and EOE-EUE classes (χ 2 = 1.59, p = .207, d = .17)", so the overall four-class replication narrative cannot be transferred to this unresolved individual effect.
